title: FX transition synthesis parameters
description: Synthesis parameters for one deterministic stereo FX transition (v0.1, proposal, #482, D-032; input: docs/research/2026-11-07_fx-transitions.md section 5). Output shape (n, 2). Only schema_version, seed and bpm are required; all lengths are in beats. Out-of-range values are rejected, never clamped. One shared parameter space for six kinds (`kind`: riser, downlifter, sweep, impact, noise_crash, reverse_crash); a kind sets the anchor rule and the DEFAULTS of the per-kind fields, never which fields exist. A field a kind does not use has no effect. PER-KIND DEFAULTS LIVE IN THIS FILE: a field whose default depends on the kind has no top-level `default`; its default for each kind is the `default` annotation inside that kind's branch of `allOf` (the riser branch also applies when `kind` is omitted, because riser is the default kind). Two fields have a derived default instead (ramp_beats and tone_glide_beats: omitted = the resolved length_beats). The engine resolves top-level defaults first, then the kind branch, then the derived ones, and the sidecar records the fully resolved object. Presets are named overrides on top of these defaults, not a second source of defaults. All ranges and defaults are PROPOSALS: only the noise_crash high-pass 1000 Hz with a 4-8 bar fade and the riser/downlifter lengths of 8/16/32 bars rest on a source (magazine tutorials, note F8/F9); every other number is a placeholder until the audio-engineer measures it and the user listens. Not part of v0.1: Shepard-style endless risers, sampled cymbals, a key or note-name resolver for the tone layer, per-layer filters, automation curves other than t^curve, a planner adapter (orchestrator, own issue).
$comment: Contract rules that JSON Schema cannot express or that are not field ranges. Time t is file time in beats from the first sample (t_s = t * 60 / bpm seconds); the beat length is 60 / bpm s. (1) Frames: the file has round((length_beats + tail_beats) * 60 * sample_rate / bpm) frames; the musical boundary is at frame round(length_beats * 60 * sample_rate / bpm) (both in double precision). Cross-field rule A: the file length (length_beats + tail_beats) * 60000 / bpm must be at most 72000 ms, so 32 bars plus the longest tail fit down to 120 BPM (measured cost at 135 BPM, 58.7 s stereo: issue #482). Anchor: riser, downlifter, sweep, impact and noise_crash start on their event beat (anchor start, boundary = end of length_beats); reverse_crash ENDS on its event beat (anchor end, the boundary is the last frame), so a placer puts its first sample at boundary - length_beats. Its tail_beats must be 0 (stated in its allOf branch). (2) Layers: a noise layer (noise_level) and a tone layer (tone_level). Cross-field rule B: noise_level and tone_level must not both be 0 (the file would be silent and the peak ceiling undefined). Noise: seeded white noise, two sub-streams s0, s1 of the seed (audio_engine.dsp.substreams; later layers take new indices, so adding a layer never changes existing noise); L = s0, R = c * s0 + sqrt(1 - c^2) * s1 with c = 1 - stereo_width (correlation 1 - stereo_width, equal power). noise_color pink = the white noise shaped in the frequency domain by sqrt(1000 / f) for f >= 20 Hz and 0 below 20 Hz, then scaled to the RMS of the white noise. The tone layer is mono (identical in both channels) and seed-independent. (3) Filter: acts on the noise layer only; the tone layer is not filtered. Every filter is ONE time-varying 2nd-order filter whose cutoff is updated every sample, not a blend of fixed filters (measurement in issue #482: a blended bank on a 3-per-octave grid shows two spectral peaks in 184 of 280 frames at band-pass Q 12, a moving filter in 0). Topology: the topology-preserving-transform state-variable filter (Zavalishin), Q = filter_q; `bp` = its band-pass output times 1 / filter_q (0 dB peak gain), `lp` = low-pass output, `hp` = high-pass output; `hp_lp` = the hp at fc followed by an lp at min(fc * lp_ratio, 0.45 * sample_rate) with Q 0.7071 (the min is a derived corner, not a clamped field). Cutoff track fc(t) = cutoff_start_hz * (cutoff_end_hz / cutoff_start_hz) ^ (p ^ sweep_curve) with p = min(1, t / length_beats); after the boundary it holds cutoff_end_hz. A static filter is cutoff_start_hz = cutoff_end_hz. For reverse_crash every curve runs in file time (start = first sample, end = boundary). (4) Level: the noise gain in dB is L(t) = level_start_db + (level_end_db - level_start_db) * min(1, t / ramp_beats) ^ level_curve, times noise_level; ramp_beats omitted = length_beats. (5) Tone: frequency f(t) = tone_start_hz * (tone_end_hz / tone_start_hz) ^ min(1, t / tone_glide_beats) (exponential glide; tone_glide_beats omitted = length_beats), phase 0 at t = 0, phase = integral of f. tone_wave sine; saw and square are band-limited (no partial at or above 0.45 * sample_rate at any time; how a partial that crosses that limit during a glide is faded is defined by the engine PR, a contract-change then); `metal` = the hat-params metal_bank partial set (205.3, 304.4, 369.6, 522.7, 540 and 800 Hz band-limited squares, hat-params $comment point 2) scaled by f(t) / 205.3. Tone envelope: tone_decay_beats 0 = the same dB curve L(t) as the noise; tone_decay_beats > 0 = an exponential fall of 60 dB over tone_decay_beats from t = 0 (L(t) is then not applied to the tone), times tone_level. (6) Dry end: the dry signal (noise + tone) ends at boundary - cut_beats with a 5 ms linear fade-out that ends there; after that only the echo and reverb tails sound ('hangover', note F8). Cross-field rule C: cut_beats must be smaller than length_beats. (7) Order: dry layers -> drive (the kick's anti-aliased saturation, per channel; 0 = off) -> echo (audio_engine.laser_fx.echo_v2 semantics, delay = note_ms(echo_note, bpm), echo_mix 0 = off) -> plus reverb_mix * reverb (laser_fx.reverb_wet semantics: energy-matched wet, reverb_mix 0 = off) -> pump -> peak scaling -> 5 ms linear fade-out at the end of the file. For reverse_crash the whole chain up to and including the reverb is rendered in forward time and then reversed in time, and all level, cutoff and tone curves are given in FILE time (after the reversal): its default level_start_db -60 -> level_end_db 0 is the swell that ends on the boundary. (8) Pump: gain 1 - pump_depth * (1 - phi)^4, phi = position inside the current beat in [0, 1), counted from the first sample for anchor start and backwards from the last sample for anchor end; 0 = off. (9) Peak: the whole file is scaled so the peak of the QUANTISED file is peak_ceiling_dbfs within one LSB and never above (normalisation after the level ramp keeps the ramp's shape; the absolute level vs a kick is therefore a property of the final file and is measured there). (10) Determinism: same resolved parameters (including seed) give a byte-identical WAV on every CI platform; the tone layer at noise_level 0 is seed-independent. (11) Reject out-of-range values, never clamp. Reject cross-field rules A, B and C with an error text. Defaults are placeholders until measured. (12) Sidecar: category 'fx', schema_version 0.2, engine.name 'abeltongod-audio-engine-fx' with the fx engine's own version (sample-metadata.schema.json, D-025); features additionally carry boundary_frame and anchor. Shared field names keep the meaning of laser-params v0.2 (seed, variants, bpm, sample_rate, bit_depth, stereo_width, reverb_*, echo_mix, echo_feedback, echo_damp_hz, echo_pingpong, preset) and kick-params (drive, peak_ceiling_dbfs); echo_note is new (laser's echo_sync has an 'off' value, here echo_mix 0 is off).

seed.description: Seeds the noise layer (sub-streams s0, s1). Same parameters and seed give a byte-identical WAV.

bpm.description: Required: every length is in beats.

kind.description: Sets the anchor rule ($comment point 1) and the per-kind defaults (allOf). reverse_crash ends on its event beat; all others start on it.

length_beats.description: Musical length in beats (per-kind default). Riser: the build it spans. The file is length_beats + tail_beats long (cross-field rule A: at most 72000 ms).

tail_beats.description: Echo/reverb tail after the boundary, beats (per-kind default). Must be 0 for reverse_crash.

cut_beats.description: The dry signal ends this many beats before the boundary (a riser into a pre-drop gap); the tails still run. 0 = off. Must be smaller than length_beats (cross-field rule C).

peak_ceiling_dbfs.description: Peak of the quantised file after scaling ($comment point 9). -1.0 by default (more headroom than the drums' -0.3; proposal).

stereo_width.description: 0 = both noise channels identical; 1 = independent L/R noise (correlation 1 - stereo_width). The tone layer is always mono.

drive.description: Anti-aliased saturation on the dry layers, same stage as kick drive, per channel. 0 = off.

pump_depth.description: Level dip on every beat, phase-locked to the anchor ($comment point 8). 0 = off.

noise_level.description: Noise layer gain. 0 = no noise (then tone_level must be above 0, cross-field rule B).

noise_color.description: pink = white shaped by sqrt(1000 / f) above 20 Hz ($comment point 2).

filter_mode.description: Noise filter (per-kind default): one time-varying 2nd-order state-variable filter ($comment point 3). hp_lp = hp at the cutoff, then lp at cutoff * lp_ratio.

cutoff_start_hz.description: Cutoff (bp: centre; hp_lp: the hp corner) at t = 0 (per-kind default).

cutoff_end_hz.description: Cutoff at the boundary; above or below the start (per-kind default). Equal to the start = static filter.

lp_ratio.description: hp_lp only: lp corner / hp corner.

filter_q.description: Q of the state-variable filter (bp: centre / bandwidth). Per-kind default in allOf where it differs from 1.2. Resonance adds a whistle (note F4); at which Q it becomes audible is not established.

sweep_curve.description: Log-frequency position of the cutoff = p ^ sweep_curve; above 1 = late rise. Per-kind default in allOf where it differs from 1.

level_start_db.description: Noise level at t = 0, dB (per-kind default).

level_end_db.description: Noise level at t = ramp_beats and after, dB (per-kind default).

level_curve.description: dB position of the level ramp = (t / ramp_beats) ^ level_curve.

ramp_beats.description: Duration of the level ramp, beats. Omitted = length_beats (derived default); impact has its own default (a short noise burst). Longer than length_beats is allowed: the boundary is then reached before the end level.

tone_wave.description: Tone waveform (per-kind default). saw and square band-limited; metal = the hat metal_bank partials ($comment point 5).

tone_start_hz.description: Tone frequency at t = 0 (metal: the lowest partial), Hz (per-kind default).

tone_end_hz.description: Tone frequency at t = tone_glide_beats and after, Hz (per-kind default).

tone_glide_beats.description: Duration of the exponential glide, beats. Omitted = length_beats (derived default); impact has its own default.

tone_decay_beats.description: 0 = the tone follows the noise level ramp; above 0 = the tone falls 60 dB over this many beats from t = 0 (per-kind default).

reverb_mix.description: Relative send level of the reverb (1 = wet energy equals dry energy), as laser v0.2 (per-kind default). 0 = off.

reverb_decay_ms.description: Reverb decay as laser v0.2 reverb_decay_ms, extended to 8000 ms (laser validated up to 6000). Default 3000 (note F4: 'about 3 s').

echo_mix.description: Level of the first echo tap relative to the dry signal. 0 = off.

echo_feedback.description: Level ratio between successive echo taps. No effect at echo_mix 0.

echo_damp_hz.description: One-pole damping of each echo tap, as laser v0.2 (20000 = off). Default 6000 here (laser: 20000).

echo_note.description: Echo delay as a note value at bpm (audio_engine.laser_fx.note_ms). No 'off': echo_mix 0 is off.

preset.description: Name of the preset these values came from, if any.

allOf.$comment: riser defaults; also applies when kind is omitted (riser is the default kind)
